keyVerseText: So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb חָדַל (châdal) is a primitive root conveying the core idea of ceasing or desisting from an action. Its literal sense involves becoming flabby or slack, which metaphorically extends to stopping, resting, or leaving off an activity. This root sense enriches the common English gloss of 'cease' by implying a deliberate halting or relaxation of effort rather than a mere pause, highlighting a transition from activity to rest or inactivity.
usageInScripture: The word חָדַל occurs 56 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently carrying the meaning of stopping or ceasing an action. It is most frequently translated as 'cease' or 'ceased,' indicating a definitive end to a process or behavior. Other translations such as 'forbear,' 'leave off,' and 'rest' show its flexibility in contexts involving refraining from action or becoming idle. This range reveals that חָדַל broadly communicates the idea of intentional discontinuation, whether of physical activity, speech, or other forms of engagement.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חָדַל deepens our grasp of biblical themes of obedience, judgment, and divine intervention. The concept of ceasing or forsaking actions can reflect human response to God's commands or the cessation of human efforts in light of divine sovereignty. In the Christian faith, the idea of resting or leaving off can also point toward the spiritual rest found in Christ, who calls believers to cease striving in their own strength. Recognizing the intentional stopping implied by חָדַל invites believers to consider when God calls them to desist from certain behaviors to trust in His providence and timing.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 11:8 states, 'So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.' Here, חָדַל underscores the cessation of the people's unified effort to build the city, marking the divine intervention that halted their project. The word highlights that the building was not merely paused but definitively stopped by God's action, emphasizing His sovereign authority to bring human plans to an end. This cessation serves as a theological reminder that God can and will interrupt human endeavors according to His purposes.
